title: Self-management for early detection of vasculitis flare-ups: a prospective study
summary:
Background:
Flare-ups in inflammatory rheumatic diseases are often detected late. Digital self-monitoring concepts could enable earlier detection and treatment.

Research question:
Can regular digital self-monitoring of symptoms and biomarkers in patients with large and small vessel vasculitis detect flare-ups at an early stage, reduce damage, and strengthen patients' self-management? Which risk factors and biomarkers are associated with flare-ups?

Methodology:
Every 4 weeks, patients complete questionnaires, urine tests, and capillary blood tests (CRP, blood sugar, blood count) at home, measure their blood pressure, and document their range of motion via photo/video. The data is transmitted via an app and monitored by a physician. In case of abnormalities, the patient is contacted promptly. In addition, biomarkers from routine blood samples are analyzed. A final interview is optional.
conditions: Giant cell arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, ANCA-associated vasculitides

interventions.name: Self-management group: digital questionnaires, independent blood sampling, urine measurements, photo/video documentation every 4 weeks, on-site appointments as part of routine care every 3-6 months
Control group: On-site visits as part of routine care every 3–6 months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of vasculitis/PMR (ICD-10: M30.1, M31.1, M31.7, M31.5, M31.4, M35.3, M35.3)
- Consent of the patient
- Patient capable of giving consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Failure to meet the inclusion criteria
